title: Verify k candidates at one node
goal:
Implement the multi-round speculative sampling step that verifies the children of one tree node (Section 3.3 and Appendix A.2).

The draft proposed `k` candidate tokens for the same position. They were drawn i.i.d. from the draft distribution `q`. The target distribution at that position is `p`.

Write `verify_node(p, q, cands, u, rng)`.

- Test the candidates in order. Candidate `i` is accepted when `u[i] <= p_cur[x] / q[x]`, where `x = cands[i]` and `p_cur` is the current target distribution.
- After each rejection, replace `p_cur` with `norm(max(0, p_cur - q))`.
- If a candidate is accepted, return `(x, i)`.
- If every candidate is rejected, draw one token from `p_cur` with `rng.choice` and return `(token, -1)`.

The tokens are Python ints. `p`, `q` are arrays of shape `(V,)`, and `u` holds `k` uniform draws from $U(0, 1)$. The starter includes `residual_distribution`.
hints: Keep a variable `cur = p` and loop over `zip(cands, u)`. Return as soon as a candidate passes.
The test uses `cur`, not the original `p`. After a rejection, set `cur = residual_distribution(cur, q)`.

After the loop, every candidate failed. Sample the replacement token from `cur`, the last adjusted distribution. Sampling from the original `p` is the common bug, and only a distribution test shows it.
Return `int(...)` values so the tests can compare them with plain integers.
